blocks.text: Data source mapping defines how data from your external vendors is translated in the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform). You can manage data source mapping to ensure that your ingested data remains accurate and aligned with the Agentic SecOps Platform data model as your security environment or vendor schemas evolve. To learn more, see Mapping Data Sources and Using Mapping Copilot.
To help you track the state of your source mappings, a status label is displayed next to the source name on its mapping page:

blocks.item: Default Mapping: The source is using a preconfigured mapping provided by Zscaler based on industry best practices.
Custom Mapping: Appears automatically when you modify any part of a default mapping. This includes adding connections, editing logic, or pasting connections from another source.
System Managed Mapping: The source is using a read-only mapping maintained by Zscaler. These mappings cannot be modified or edited.

blocks.text: When managing data source mapping, you can perform the following actions:

blocks.item: Revert to default mapping.

Some data sources include preconfigured default mapping. You can revert any custom changes to return to the original default configuration. When you revert the mapping, the source label changes from Custom Mapping to Default Mapping.
To revert to the default mapping (when supported):
In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Configure.
In the left-side navigation, click Sources.
Open the mapping page using one of the following methods:
Hover over a source, and click the Map Data icon.
Select the checkbox of a data source from the list, and click Map Data on the toolbar.
The Map <Source> page appears.
Click the More icon, and select Apply Default Mapping.
This overwrites any custom logic you created for that source.
See image.
Review the updated mapping, and click Save to apply your changes.
View audit logs.
You can track changes made to a source's mapping configuration to monitor updates and troubleshoot issues. Audit logs provide a history of who modified the mapping and when the changes occurred.
To view mapping audit logs:
In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Configure.
In the left-side navigation, click Sources.
Open the mapping page using one of the following methods:
Hover over a source, and click the Map Data icon.
Select the checkbox of a data source from the list, and click Map Data on the toolbar.
The Map <Source> page appears.
Click the More icon, and select Audit Logs.
This overwrites any custom logic you created for that source.
See image.
The Audit Logs <Source> connector page appears.
Review the mapping change history.
Copy and paste mapping connections.

You can copy an entire source mapping to use in another source. This copies the full mapping configuration (including all connections and any custom logic) and can be useful when you're onboarding similar sources.
To copy and paste a source mapping:
In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Configure.
In the left-side navigation, click Sources.
Open the mapping page for the source you want to copy:
Hover over a source, and click the Map Data icon.
Select the checkbox for a data source from the list, and click Map Data on the toolbar.
The Map <Source> page appears.
In the Mapped Connections section, click the More icon, and select Copy All Connections.
See image.
Click Cancel to return to the Sources page, and open the mapping page for the source you want to update.
In the Mapped Connections section, click the More icon, and select Paste Connections.
This replaces the current mapping of the source.
Review the updated mapping, and click Save to apply your changes.
Unmap all fields.
You can clear all existing field mappings for a source. This can be useful when you want to manually redefine the entire mapping configuration without reverting to a default setup.
To unmap all fields:
In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click Configure.
In the left-side navigation, click Sources.
Open the mapping page for the source:
Hover over a source and click the Map Data icon.
Select a checkbox for a data source from the list, and click Map Data on the toolbar.
The Map <Source> page appears.
In the Mapped Connections section, click the More icon, and select Unmap All Fields.
This removes all currently mapped connections from the mapping section.
See image.
Click Save to apply your changes.
